output.title: Spot trial expiry before it becomes a surprise
output.body:
If you run a small business, spotting trial expiry early is not a big AI project. It is a bounded workflow decision: when should an alert fire, and who needs to see it first?

Start with one diagnostic question: are your trial dates already in one place, or are they spread across email, calendars, spreadsheets, and vendor accounts? If the dates are already central, a simple reminder may be enough. If they are scattered, you may need a small integration step to collect them before anything can warn you.

Keep the decision with the owner. Automation should surface the date; it should not choose renew, downgrade, or cancel. Human approval stays in place for binding decisions and any money movement. That is the part you do not want to hand to a reminder rule.

A practical next step is to list every SaaS trial you are using and note which tool, if any, already tracks the renewal date. That inventory shows whether the work is plain monitoring or a slightly smarter workflow in your own environment. If the answer is “nowhere,” at least the mystery is smaller.
